title: Mathesar
name: mathesar
description: Spreadsheet-like interface for PostgreSQL, for browsing, editing and linking tables without SQL, building queries by pointing and clicking and importing CSVs. Runs on its own database or connects to Postgres you already have. Source: https://github.com/mathesar-foundation/mathesar

env.name: MATHESAR_DB_PASSWORD
env.label: Database password (required)
env.description: Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32. Keep it the same when you redeploy, or Mathesar can't reach its database.

env.name: MATHESAR_PORT
env.label: Host port for the web UI

note: Set the database password before you deploy (openssl rand -hex 32 makes a good one), since the stack won't start without it, and keep it the same when you redeploy. Then open http://<your-host>:8250 (or whichever port you picked) and make the admin account straight away, as whoever gets there first owns it. That page comes with two boxes ticked, a one-time install ping and anonymous usage stats, both sent to Mathesar, so untick them if you'd rather not (usage stats can also be switched off under Administration --> Settings). Connect Database --> Create a New Database makes one on the bundled Postgres, with sample data if you like, or point it at a Postgres server you already run. Your browser checks GitHub for new releases. The bundled database lives in the postgres-data volume, and the secret key that encrypts saved database passwords is made on first start in mathesar-secrets, so keep both. Docs: docs.mathesar.org
